chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
Regarding the words of Allah, Blessed is His Name,
Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.

He said: It means obligatory. And it does not mean a time of loss, such that if that time passes and he prays it, his prayer is not considered fulfilled. And if that were the case, Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them both) would have been destroyed when he prayed it outside its time. But whenever he remembered it, he prayed it.
Then he said: And whenever you are certain or doubt regarding its time that you did not pray it, or regarding its time of loss that you did not pray it, you must pray it.
If you doubt after the time of loss has passed, then an obstacle has entered, so there is no requirement for you to repeat it due to doubt until you become certain.
If you become certain, then it is upon you to pray it in whatever state you are.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up prayer if one misses its specific time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the distinction between the obligation of prayer and its specific time window, using Prophet Sulayman as a precedent to show that missing the time does not invalidate the duty. It provides a nuanced legal ruling for doubt: if one is uncertain whether the prayer was missed or performed during the time, it is considered valid, but certainty of omission requires immediate makeup (Qada) regardless of the current state. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease in worship and the preservation of ritual integrity through clear evidentiary standards.
